chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (AS): May Allah rectify you,
"The nature made by Allah is which He has made men upon"?
He (AS) said: He created them with a predisposition towards Divine Unity at the time of the Covenant, upon knowing Him that He is their Lord,
I asked: And did they address Him?
He (AS) said: He lowered his head, then said: Had it not been for that, they would not have known who is their Lord or who is their Sustainer.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fitrah in the context of the Covenant (Mithaq)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this narration within the chapter on Divine Unity to illustrate that Tawhid is not merely a theological proposition but an ontological reality embedded in the human soul since the primordial Covenant (Mithaq). The Imam’s gesture and subsequent explanation emphasize that this innate recognition is the foundational cause for humanity’s ability to identify Allah as both Lord (Rabb) and Sustainer (Raziq), distinguishing the Shia understanding of Fitrah as active, pre-temporal knowledge rather than passive instinct.
